utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. General Galic, we were informed about the reasons of your late arrival. We hope that it means that proper attention is given to your medical condition.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you, first of all, for your attention, the attention of the Chamber and the administration of the detention unit and of the specialist who treated me. Because it was made possible for me to get what I needed most. If you will allow me I will say it. This was a routine examination at the specialist and we spoke to him about the evolution of my sickness and the problems connected to it. And we had consultations. I asked him questions and got answers, so I will not burden you with that, unless of course you are interested, in which case, I can tell you. Basically my state has deteriorated slightly, but we have remained on this that I will take it as long as I can until the operation is carried out. That is in a nutshell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, we cannot change your condition. The only thing we can do is to take care that proper attention is paid to your condition. So I do understand that this is the case. Apart from that, I would like to know whether you feel fit enough to continue at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel capable of continuing. For the time being, there are no problems, but you have told me that I should inform you if I have problems and that you will rule and I will stick by what you said. But, I hope, as you can see, what I am like, so I hope that I will be able to continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General Galic. Please be seated. Ms. Pilipovic, the Chamber still owes you a response to the objection made yesterday, objection to the admission into evidence of the report of the expert witness, Dr. Turner. The report of the expert witness, Dr. Turner, is admitted into evidence. The expert has, in general terms, given his opinion on what would be relevant factors to cause extreme fear, being extreme fear the main element of the definition he used for the concept of terror. He explained different levels of fear. He further elaborated on the symptoms and disorders caused by and the response of human beings to a state of extreme fear. He paid attention to the recovery from such fear and elaborated on what type of action would potentially contribute to the induction of extreme fear. Part of the report gives information on what other scholars in the field have published on fear, mainly in relation to posttraumatic stress disorders they observed sometimes specifically to in a situation of war. The expert has been provided with descriptions of the events in Sarajevo, such as contained in the indictment and extracts of some of the evidence presented to this Chamber. The expert has used this information to select the type of events he concentrated on in the parts of his report where he more specifically links such type of events to the effect it might have on a civilian population in a situation of war. If the events as described in the material the expert was provided with would in part or in its entirety be proven these parts of the report could assist to that extent the Chamber in its understanding of the evidence presented to it. The Defence has had the opportunity to bring whatever it deemed to be relevant, additional type of facts, to the attention of the expert witness and ask him what effect such type of facts would have on his findings. The Chamber will consider what probative value the expert report has and will take into careful consideration to what extent the type of facts, at least where the expert based his opinion on such type of facts, in reality occurred in Sarajevo. This concerns the evaluation of the evidence and does not effect its admissibility. That is the ruling on the expert report of Dr. Turner. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that I should raise this point since we are going to speak about another one of your decisions. These are to do with the keeping of the transcripts, to draw the attention of the booths and of the Chamber to what Dr. Turner said, apparently was badly translated but of course I am not an expert to the matter. I am referring to the page 104, line 22, if you will allow me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in line 22, Mr. Turner said in French and I am going to quote in French: "What I said in the times of war, the civilians who are involved in the war, if these civilians die near a military target or killed near a military target, perhaps they will be affected by this experience." And so on and so on. It goes without saying that here this is a contradiction, a surprising contradiction, and there are a number of these. And I wanted to draw the attention to this one. It seems obvious that if we die, we are going to be affected, but we have to be extremely careful about the equivalence of the transcripts. For this reason, I should have intervened last time, but I didn't, because I was focussing on what the witness was saying. I thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you check the original English transcript because it is now translated again, your words now in English, and what you actually say is that once you died, you might not experience anything any more. But did you also check what was in the original English text so that we can now clarify the issue. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. The meaning is not much clearer in the language of the witness but it is comprehensible in English, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it would be the same in French and English, and both incomprehensible for you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not at all, it is comprehensible in English and it was a problem seemingly in relation to the interpretation. But it is perfectly acceptable or relatively acceptable in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your clarification. I will try to look it up, but I have different pages now, looking back to the transcript of yesterday. But I will try to find it and check the English words used by the expert witness. Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, two things before that happens. Firstly, I have the redacted report of Mr. Zecevic to be tendered. Mr. Stamp is present to speak to that, if required. A copy has been provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes and no, Mr. President. Yes and no, because what I am being told here is not quite the truth. This document has not been redacted. It has not been redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please try to solve that during the next break and then I take it that the Chamber will be provided with the redacted --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We will speak to Mr. Piletta-Zanin during the next break and no doubt be the wiser for the experience. Mr. President, I understand that Mr. Piletta-Zanin wants to raise an issue that will take some five minutes before we call Witness AD. So perhaps, if he wishes to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, the Defence received recently four new statements --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. But in anticipation of what my friend might be about to discuss, given the reference to the number "four" I wonder if this is appropriately dealt with in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we are not yet in closed question. I don't see closed session on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should speak more clearly, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand, you would like to raise the matter being raised in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well it depends on -- well, I do not know the content. If it is about witnesses that are protected, then we preferably should do so. If not -- Mr. Ierace, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the issue that Mr. Piletta-Zanin wishes to raise concerns four statements which were disclosed to him yesterday, I think it appropriate that that be dealt with in closed session because it inevitable will raise an issue which would clearly require a closed session hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you agree, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not sure to which extent this witness is -- witnesses who will be protected by any measures. Could Mr. Ierace perhaps give us some more information, however little it may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... whether it should be in closed session or not, in closed session, and if what Mr. Ierace tells us would not convince the Chamber that it should be dealt with in closed session we return to open session and then deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will now turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: s f

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President I have a timetable issue to raise. The Prosecution was informed earlier today that the artillery expert, Mr. Kovac, is no longer available on the 29th and 30th of July. That necessitates us proposing an earlier date, and we have in mind the 10th and if the Trial Chamber is sitting, the 12th of July. It is difficult for the Prosecution to arrange a date for this witness because of his particular interpretation requirements. He will give his evidence in the Hungarian language. Therefore, we thought it prudent to alert the Trial Chamber to our proposal, and indeed the Defence, since the Defence will presumably want to have its expert attend on the same date as Mr. Kovac. So, Mr. President, I would be very grateful if the Defence could advise us by, say, tomorrow if that date is suitable to their expert so that we can arrange for a Hungarian interpreter to be available on those dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you be able to inform by tomorrow whether the 10th and/or perhaps the 12th of July would be suitable for your expert?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was you suggested on the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As we indicated before, Mr. Ierace, whether the 12th will be available or not, we will only know by the end of this week. So the 10th we will be sitting, but whether we also will be sitting on the 12th is still uncertain. Yes. Then, if the Prosecution would be ready to call the next witness, we will now turn into closed session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 7.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
